headline: Quiet on the street through Sunday afternoon: every model keeps the wettest 3 hours under 0.1 in, the channel is at base flow, and the king tides are a Bay-shore concern only; NWS now expects Sunday's cold front to bring moderate, briefly heavy rain Sunday into Sunday night.

summary.text: Coastal Flood Warning ended at 4 PM, replaced by an Advisory through 5 PM Sunday. NWS now calls Sunday's cold front moderate with brief heavy rain, Sunday into Sunday night, mostly past this window.
Wettest 3 hours, next 72 h (to 3 PM Sunday): ECMWF 0.09, NBM 0.05, RRFS 0.04, GFS 0.01 in; HRRR 15-minute 0.00 in. HRRR hourly returned no data again.
Rating card consensus (RRFS and NBM; HRRR missing) about 0.05 in: none. Yellow (garage) would need about 0.71 in in 3 hours.
Friday 9.1 ft high at 1:28 PM, NOAA model about 10.2 ft. Saturday 8.6 ft at 2:27 PM. Channel at Alameda 0.12 ft, far below Monitoring 3.18 ft.
Nothing needed on the street. Use the dry Friday and Saturday to clear drain grates and leaves before Sunday night's front. Avoid the Bay shore around midday high tides.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text:
A ridge of high pressure keeps the area dry and mild through Saturday, with high clouds, highs in the 60s to lower 70s, and patchy night and morning fog (NWS San Francisco, 12:21 PM and 1:21 PM discussion). NWS calls Saturday the last dry day of the next seven.

Saturday night into early Sunday a warm front spreads light to moderate rain north to south; the stronger cold front follows Sunday into Sunday night with moderate to brief periods of heavy rain and breezier winds (not Wind Advisory strength), plus a 10 to 15 % thunderstorm chance in the North Bay. That is a step up in wording from this morning, when NWS described Sunday's system as weak, but it gave no rainfall amounts this afternoon. A colder second storm follows Monday through midweek on a more southern track, with the heaviest rain on the Central Coast, less over the Bay Area, and possible Wind Advisories.

sections.title: Model trends
sections.text:
From 4 PM Thursday to 3 PM Sunday, wettest 3 hours / total:
• HRRR hourly: no data in this snapshot.
• RRFS: 0.04 / 0.05 in (early Sunday afternoon).
• NBM: 0.05 / 0.08 in (late Sunday morning).
• ECMWF: 0.09 / 0.20 in (late Sunday morning), the wettest.
• GFS: 0.01 / 0.01 in.
• HRRR 15-minute (ends 11:45 PM Fri): 0.00 in.

All models start the rain Sunday morning and keep it light through mid-afternoon; GFS holds most of it until early Sunday evening (0.04 in at 7 PM). The cold front NWS highlights for Sunday night is just past the 72-hour window and past the end of these model series, so it is not yet in the numbers. Expect the next runs to show it.

sections.title: Tide and the channel
sections.text:
NOAA's Bay model (run ends 1 PM Saturday) is running about 0.8 to 1.1 ft above predicted highs at Redwood City. Today's 9.4 ft king tide at 12:35 PM was modeled near 10.4 ft around 1 PM. Friday: 7.1 ft at 3:02 AM (about 8.1 ft) and 9.1 ft at 1:28 PM (about 10.2 ft near 1:45 PM). Saturday: 7.1 ft at 3:56 AM (about 8.2 ft) and 8.6 ft at 2:27 PM. Sunday: 7.2 ft at 4:49 AM and 7.9 ft at 3:33 PM, with the light rain falling around that afternoon high.

NWS Coastal Flood Advisory (3:35 PM) for Bayshore locations until 5 PM Sunday: up to 1.7 ft of inundation in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways, with the San Francisco gauge 1.7 ft above normal Friday, 1.6 ft Saturday and 0.9 ft Sunday, including up to 1.3 ft of surge. This affects the Bay shore and tidal sloughs, not Athlone Terrace directly.

Channel at Alameda de las Pulgas: 0.12 ft at 4 PM, flat between 0.10 and 0.14 ft for the past day (Monitoring 3.18 ft, Watch 4.6 ft, Warning 5.65 ft). Upstream of Caltrain: 0.07 ft at its latest report, 5:13 AM today (Monitoring 2.8 ft).

sections.title: Current observations
sections.text: Dry. The Caltrain rain gauge showed no rain in the 24 hours to its 5:13 AM report; it is still reporting only about every 12 hours. The hourly Alameda channel gauge is steady at base flow.

sections.title: What to do
sections.text:
• Nothing needed on the street through Saturday; no need to move cars.
• Friday or Saturday: clear leaves from street drain grates and yard drains, and check sandbags and flashlights ahead of Sunday night's front and next week's windier storm.
• Stay off the Bay shore, piers and low shoreline roads around the midday high tides through Sunday, and don't walk or drive through moving water.
